name: Battle of Mohács
note: The accounts do not give compass directions, so none is drawn. The Hungarians are drawn on the left and the Ottomans on the right. Where the marsh and the Csele stream lay is not stated: they are placed behind the Hungarian line, where the story needs them, and the village of Mohács is not drawn. The Ottoman wings and the Janissaries are placed by judgement, since the accounts say only that the counterattack came from both wings and that the Janissaries and artillery fired from prepared positions. The accounts put the Ottoman strength at perhaps 45,000 fighting troops, or perhaps 50,000, with some historians saying 100,000. One report has Suleiman struck on his cuirass by bullets during the charge; the plan does not show it. King Louis's flight is drawn only in the last phase, by a small block placed beside the marsh; the accounts do not say where he left the field.

phases.title: The two armies take up their positions
phases.text: The Hungarians stood in two lines on a waterlogged plain, mercenary infantry and artillery in the centre of the first with heavy cavalry on both flanks, and levy infantry and reserve cavalry behind. The Ottomans faced them with Ibrahim Pasha in the centre.
phases.quote: The Hungarian army, numbering around 25,000–30,000 men, was arranged in two lines: the first composed of mercenary infantry and artillery in the centre, with heavy cavalry on both flanks; the second consisted largely of levy infantry and reserve cavalry.

phases.title: The Hungarian cavalry charges the Ottoman front
phases.text: In the early afternoon Archbishop Pál Tomori led a charge that drove back the Ottoman front line and caused disorder among the irregulars. The Ottoman centre gave ground.
phases.quote: In the early afternoon, Archbishop Pál Tomori led a charge that initially drove back the Ottoman front line, causing disorder among the irregulars.

phases.title: The Ottoman centre falls back in a crescent
phases.text: Ibrahim Pasha's centre fell back in a controlled manoeuvre and formed a crescent. This exposed the flanks of the advancing Hungarian cavalry.
phases.quote: Ibrahim Pasha's centre fell back in a controlled manoeuvre, forming a crescent that exposed the flanks of the advancing Hungarian cavalry.

phases.title: King Louis and the reserves move in support
phases.text: King Louis and the reserves moved forward in support of the Hungarian cavalry, which had advanced past the Ottoman centre.
phases.quote: As King Louis and the reserves moved in support

phases.title: The Ottoman wings counterattack and the guns open fire
phases.text: The Ottomans struck with cavalry and light infantry from both wings, while Janissaries and artillery fired from prepared positions. The Hungarian army had advanced too far and too fast.
phases.quote: the Ottomans launched a counterattack with cavalry and light infantry from both wings, while Janissaries and artillery opened concentrated fire from prepared positions.

phases.title: The Hungarian army is encircled and its lines collapse
phases.text: Surrounded and under concentrated musket and cannon fire, the Hungarian army collapsed within two hours. Over 14,000 Hungarian troops died by one estimate.
phases.quote: The Hungarian army, having advanced too far and too fast, found itself encircled and subjected to concentrated musket and cannon fire. Within two hours, their lines collapsed.

phases.title: King Louis flees and drowns near the Csele
phases.text: King Louis II tried to flee from the collapsing army but drowned in the marshy ground near the Csele stream, weighed down by his armour.
phases.quote: King Louis II attempted to flee but drowned in the marshy terrain near the Csele stream, weighed down by his armour.
